transcript:
User: Hi, I saw your ad about missed calls. We lose calls after hours and I'm curious how it works.
Agent: Got it, yeah, that ad is all about stopping those after-hours calls from turning into lost customers.  

So when someone calls after you’re closed right now and no one picks up…what actually happens to that caller — do they usually leave a voicemail, or just move on to the next place?
User: They usually leave a voicemail, but some might move on.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense — the ones who move on are the ones that sting.  

So to get a feel for the impact: roughly how many after-hours calls would you say you get in a typical week that end up as voicemails or missed entirely?
User: About 15 missed calls go to voicemail each week.
Agent: Got it, 15 a week is a lot of people trying to give you business.  

So I can picture this better, what kind of business are you running — what industry are you in?
User: I'm in the auto repair industry, running a shop called 'Precision Auto Care' in Austin, TX.
Agent: Nice, Precision Auto Care in Austin — got it.  

Has anyone ever actually walked you through what those 15 missed calls a week could be costing you in real dollars, or has it mostly just been a gut feeling that it hurts?
User: It's mostly been a gut feeling, but I suspect it impacts our revenue since around 60% would book if answered.
Agent: Mhm, that helps — 60% is a big chunk of real jobs.  

To make this concrete, what’s your average repair order look like on those kinds of calls — more like $400, $650, $850?
User: Our average job value is about $450 for those calls.
Agent: So with your numbers, those missed calls work out to about seventeen and a half grand a month in jobs that *could* be booked if someone picked up.  

Since you asked how it works: would it be helpful if I walk you through, at a high level, what happens to a caller when they ring Precision Auto after hours with our system on?
User: Yes, I'd appreciate a walkthrough of what happens with your system when someone calls after hours.
Agent: Makes sense, let’s keep it simple.  

So, picture this: it’s 8:30 pm, you’re closed, and someone calls Precision Auto Care — are you more interested in making sure they can *book an appointment right then*, or mainly that they can *leave a detailed message* so you can call them back?
User: I'm more interested in making sure they can book an appointment right then.
Agent: Got it, so priority one is: if they’re ready to book, they can lock in a slot on the spot.  

So here’s what our system does for you after hours: it answers like your front desk, talks to the caller in normal conversation, grabs what car they drive and what they need, then actually books them straight into your calendar for an open time — would you also want it to send them a confirmation text so they’re less likely to no-show?
User: Yes, a confirmation text would be helpful to reduce no-shows.
Agent: Perfect, that’s exactly how most shops use it.  

So…given you’re losing around seventeen and a half thousand a month from those missed calls, it probably makes sense to see this live — we do a 20‑minute walkthrough where we show you exactly how it would work at Precision Auto and what your numbers look like with it on; what’s better for you for that — later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow works for me. What times do you have available for the live call?
Agent: Great, tomorrow it is.  

Before we lock in a time with Jay, let me grab a couple details — what’s your first name?
User: My name is Danny, and I'm with 'Precision Auto Care'.
Agent: Nice to meet you, Danny.  

And what’s your last name, just so we book this under the right person?
Agent: Nice, thanks Danny.  

For tomorrow, I can get you in as soon as Wednesday at 11:30 or 1:45 Central — which one works better for you?
User: Reyes.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that on the calendar for you.
Agent: Alright Danny, you’re all set — I’ve got you booked with Jay this Wednesday at 11:30 Central. You’ll get a text in a bit with the confirmation and a link in case you need to reschedule. Really glad we got this set up for Precision Auto Care. If anything comes up, you can just reply to that text. Have a great rest of your day, Danny. Bye for now!
